title: Quiz: Effect of Concentration on Rate

questions.stem: What happens to the rate of reaction when the concentration of a reactant is increased?

options.text: The rate decreases
The reaction stops
The rate increases
The rate stays the same

questions.explanation: Increasing the concentration of a reactant increases the rate of reaction because there are more reactant particles per unit volume, leading to more frequent successful collisions.

questions.stem: In terms of particles, what does a higher concentration mean?

options.text: Fewer particles in a smaller volume
More particles in the same volume
Larger particles in the same volume
The same number of particles moving faster

questions.explanation: A higher concentration means there are more reactant particles packed into the same volume of solution, so the particles are closer together on average.

questions.stem: For gas reactions, which factor has a similar effect to increasing concentration in solutions?

options.text: Increasing the surface area
Decreasing the temperature
Adding a catalyst
Increasing the pressure

questions.explanation: Increasing pressure in gas reactions squeezes the same number of particles into a smaller volume, which has the same effect as increasing concentration: more particles per unit volume and more frequent collisions.

questions.stem: A student investigates the reaction between hydrochloric acid and magnesium ribbon. Which change would increase the rate of gas production?

options.text: Cooling the acid before use
Using a higher concentration of hydrochloric acid
Using a lower concentration of hydrochloric acid
Using a longer piece of magnesium ribbon

questions.explanation: Using a higher concentration of hydrochloric acid provides more H+ ions per unit volume, increasing the frequency of collisions with magnesium and therefore increasing the rate of gas production.

questions.stem: On a graph of volume of gas produced vs time, how would a higher concentration experiment compare to a lower concentration one?

options.text: The line would be steeper initially but reach the same final volume
The line would start flat and then become steep
The line would be less steep and reach a lower final volume
The line would be identical

questions.explanation: A higher concentration produces a steeper initial gradient (faster rate) but reaches the same final volume of gas, assuming the same amount of limiting reactant is used.

questions.stem: Why does the rate of reaction decrease as the reaction proceeds, even though the concentration was initially high?

options.text: The reactant particles get used up, reducing the concentration over time
The particles slow down as the reaction continues
The temperature of the mixture decreases
The catalyst stops working

questions.explanation: As the reaction proceeds, reactant particles are used up. This means fewer particles remain in the same volume, so the concentration decreases and collisions become less frequent.

questions.stem: In a fair test investigating the effect of concentration on rate, which variable must be kept constant?

options.text: The temperature of the reactants
The time taken for the reaction
The volume of gas produced
The concentration of the acid

questions.explanation: In a fair test, all variables except the one being investigated (concentration) must be kept constant. Temperature is a key control variable because it also affects rate.
